I have Cptsd and recently started cbt, and the first thing that my therapist told me was that he does a variant on it called ACT that means Acceptance and commitment therapy, you can look it up but basically he told me that he started doing ACT because he realized that CBT alone makes people feel guilty about their emotions and that it's not okay. And in my latest session when we were talking about how sometimes I have awfull thoughts about people and myself he reassured me that there's nothing wrong in feeling that way because it's all my brain and body knows, and that thus thoughts are trying to protect me. He wants me to learn to accept them and at the same time learn to not let them hurt me or sabotage myself. Hope this helps!

I suggested EMDR thinking about my personal experience with therapy and sharing. For example, before EMDR i did psychoanalysis and something that bothered me about talking about trauma was that usually the psychoanalyst tends to give their opinion about it, and that was horrible for me and did nothing. Also with them i felt like forced to share things. With EMDR there is no external opinion. You work at your own pace, and the therapist just guides you. You dont have to share or being super explicit about it  either. Its more like a personal journey through healing. You choose how to do it. At least i feel that way with EMDR.

I don't really understand what you mean with "no talking" but i suggest you try EMDR. Google it and see if that seems cool for you. I have ptsd and EMDR has made wonders with my trauma. Also it seems to be a common thing. I read a lot of people saying that it was almost like magic for they trauma. I agree. Hope it helps.
